question: With adequate data (32 templates/word instead of 4), does the Hopfield Lexical Snap refine a prototype readout?

config.control: per-sample BLOCK permutation (content destroyed, statistically matched)

d48_diagnostic.why: G-B4 returned EXACTLY 0.0000 at t=1,2,3. Exact zero is stronger than below-threshold. Two readings: (a) codebook rows are already fixed points (mechanism), or (b) the update barely moves (defect making G-B4 vacuous). Measured rather than asserted.
d48_diagnostic.conclusion: Reading (a). The representation MOVES substantially (rel 1.08 at t=1) while the argmax NEVER flips. Mechanism: at beta=26.10 softmax(beta*S) is near one-hot, so Z <- M_k (the nearest prototype); re-reading a prototype returns that prototype's own class. The refinement is structurally a fixed-point map for the readout. G-B4 is therefore vacuous by DESIGN at any beta >> 1, not by defect of this run.

bearing_on_the_blueprint.claim_tested: sec 2.4 items 1-2: replace flat linear decoders with a Continuous Modern Hopfield Network (Lexical Snap) at beta*=26.10
bearing_on_the_blueprint.finding: The class-mean codebook works and is TRAINING-FREE (0.9883 held-out, 63.2x chance, control 0.0176). Adding the specified iterative Hopfield refinement at beta*=26.10 changes nothing, for a structural reason.
bearing_on_the_blueprint.third_independent_confirmation: beta*=26.10 is argmax-invariant. Earlier: (1) k-beta probe BETA_INVARIANT across 0.5..1000; (2) typed-manifold G-B5 self-check; now (3) fully-powered V=64 Option B, 0/512 argmax flips across three refine steps.
bearing_on_the_blueprint.not_claimed: This does not show Hopfield associative memory fails in general. It shows the blueprint's SPECIFIED configuration (class-mean codebook + beta*=26.10 + softmax iteration) is equivalent to nearest-prototype lookup.

honest_limits: typed-domain labels on REAL codec waves. Not corpus facts.
single template family; synthetic word list. Not natural language.
CPU only. No GPU claim. No latency claim.
V=64, one seed. The prototype/refinement split is structural (0/512 flips), not a marginal effect, so seed sensitivity is unlikely to matter here -- but it is one seed.
